Did you know Flexygo's AI can search for information on Google?
docs.text: From the agent's configuration, you can enable the Can access Web option to allow real-time automatic Google searches.

docs.title: Key feature
docs.text: Once this setting is enabled, users can ask the agent to run web queries. An example: "Search Google for information about Flexygo".

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI can insert records for an object?
Did you know Flexygo's AI can insert records for an object?
docs.text:
Flexygo lets you automate record creation through its AI functionality. To enable this feature, two configurations are required:

  1. In the agent's configuration: enable the Can call processes option
  2. In the assistant's "Flow Processing" step: select which object and properties your agent can insert

For example, with these settings enabled you can ask your assistant to register a location.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI lets you query data without knowing SQL?
Did you know Flexygo's AI lets you query data without knowing SQL?
docs.text: You can use Flexygo's AI functionality to access data without needing to know SQL.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
To implement this feature, you must:

  1. Go to the agent's configuration
  2. Enable the Can Access DB option
  3. Define which tables and fields the user will have access to

Once configured, the agent will be able to answer questions by automatically querying those tables in real time.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI can run processes from a conversation?
Did you know Flexygo's AI can run processes from a conversation?
docs.text: Flexygo lets you automate process execution through conversations with AI.

docs.title: Configuration instructions
docs.text:
Go to your agent's settings and enable Can Call Processes to link the Flexygo processes you want to run from conversations.

This feature enables interactions such as asking the agent "Create a customer named Ahora with phone 666 666 666", and the system will register it automatically.

docs.title: Did you know you can set usage limits for Flexygo's AI assistants?
Did you know you can set usage limits for Flexygo's AI assistants?
docs.text:
From the agent list you can limit users' token usage for AI assistants by role. This feature lets administrators manage and control users' token spend according to their role within the system.

Flexygo lets you set consumption restrictions for AI assistants' tokens. These limits are configured at the user role level, providing granular control over resource and budget usage.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Restricting token usage limits helps organizations to:

  • Control the spend associated with AI assistants
  • Manage resource consumption per user
  • Implement usage policies based on organizational role

docs.title: Did you know you can see the monthly token usage for Flexygo's AI assistants?
Did you know you can see the monthly token usage for Flexygo's AI assistants?
docs.text:
From the agent list you can review the monthly token usage for AI assistants, broken down by user. This feature lets administrators monitor and control the resource spend associated with using AI assistants.

The Flexygo platform lets you view token consumption metrics on a monthly basis, making it easier to manage and oversee the use of AI tools at the individual user level.

docs.title: Did you know you can attach an AI agent to a Flexygo toolbar?
Did you know you can attach an AI agent to a Flexygo toolbar?
docs.text:
To integrate an AI agent into a Flexygo toolbar, follow these steps:

  1. Go to the toolbar where you want to add the agent
  2. Create a new button of the corresponding type
  3. Select the agent you want to launch
  4. Confirm the configuration

Once this process is complete, you will be able to access, from that module, an agent capable of:

  • Running processes
  • Querying the database
  • Searching the internet
  • Accessing your document management (if configured to do so)

docs.title: Did you know you can talk directly to the app's AI?
Did you know you can talk directly to the app's AI?
docs.text:
In addition to the flexygo.nav.goAI function available in the Flexygo application, there is an additional function called flexygo.ai.startVoiceRecognition.

This function only requires you to specify the assistant's identifier. Once enabled, it shows a modal that starts listening to what the user says. Once the audio capture is finished, the message is automatically sent to the AI assistant so it can provide its response.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's API can accept collections?
Did you know Flexygo's API can accept collections?
docs.text:
Flexygo's API has a notable capability: it can process multiple records at once. When an array of objects is sent instead of a single object, the system tries to insert each item independently.

An important safety feature is that if a problem arises during the process, the API will have tried to insert each of them independently. If any problem occurs, it will roll back all the changes made, guaranteeing data integrity.

This transactional behavior protects the database against partial inserts, ensuring that either every operation completes successfully, or none of them are applied.

docs.title: Did you know you can make Flexygo's searches accent-insensitive?
Did you know you can make Flexygo's searches accent-insensitive?
docs.text: Flexygo has a setting called SearchDbCollation that lets you customize how searches are performed on the platform.

docs.title: Main feature
docs.text: Without any additional configuration, the system uses its default behavior. However, administrators can set specific values such as Modern_Spanish_CI_AI to change the search behavior.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
By enabling this setting with a case- and accent-insensitive collation, users can:

  • Search without worrying about capitalization
  • Skip accented characters during searches
  • Find results regardless of how the information was originally recorded

This feature applies to search screens and combo fields throughout the application.

docs.title: Did you know pressing ALT lets you view property names?
Did you know pressing ALT lets you view property names?
docs.text: You can quickly view the actual names of properties while configuring them for an object in the wizard.

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text: To view property names, hover the cursor over any property's label and hold down the ALT key. This action will automatically reveal the properties' actual identifiers instead of their descriptions or visible labels.

docs.title: Did you know you can link Flexygo to a BI tool or any other system very easily?
Did you know you can link Flexygo to a BI tool or any other system very easily?
docs.text: Linking Flexygo with Business Intelligence tools or external systems is a straightforward process.

docs.title: Main steps
docs.text:
1. Enable Friendly URLs on the objects you want to link, using the corresponding checkbox
  2. Generate links with the format: Text Only
    https://crm.myflexygo.com/view/crm_cliente/25
  3. Simple integration: generate these links from any software and open them in the browser

docs.title: Additional information
docs.text: For more information, with every access possibility, check the built-in help at Help → Information → Friendly Urls.

docs.title: Did you know there's a parameter to set the browser window's title pattern?
Did you know there's a parameter to set the browser window's title pattern?
docs.text: Starting with version 4.9.0.x, Flexygo offers a new setting called WindowsNameStructure that lets you customize the browser window's title using specific patterns.

docs.title: Available placeholders
docs.text:
The setting accepts the following variables:

  • {{ObjectDescrip}}: shows the object's description, if it exists
  • {{PageDescrip}}: shows the object's description or, failing that, the page's description
  • {{ProyectName}}: shows the project's name

docs.title: Benefit
docs.text: This feature lets you change browser window titles to provide more relevant and contextual information about their content, improving the user experience and navigation within the Flexygo platform.

docs.title: Did you know you can change how many records at a time the app fetches for an object?
Did you know you can change how many records at a time the app fetches for an object?
docs.text: From an object's configuration, you can adjust the number of records retrieved during synchronization. This parameter, called the buffer size, has a direct impact on the process's performance.

docs.title: Changing the buffer size
docs.text:
To make the adjustment, you just need to modify the property called buffer size. The benefits vary depending on the configuration:

  • Larger buffers: allow faster synchronization by processing multiple records per iteration
  • Smaller buffers: recommended for tables with large or complex records

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text: Best practice suggests using a smaller buffer size when working with tables that contain heavy or complex records, avoiding errors or performance issues. In contrast, for lighter tables, a larger size can be used to optimize synchronization speed without risking overload.

docs.title: Did you know you can mention other users in the chatter?
Did you know you can mention other users in the chatter?
docs.text: Since Flexygo version 4.11.0.x, users can mention other application participants in the chatter using the @ symbol.

docs.title: Main feature
docs.text: This lets you insert references to other users by typing "@" followed by the user's name in the chatter. When someone is mentioned this way, the system automatically sends a notification alert to the referenced user.

docs.title: Did you know that in Flexygo you can set the Cl@ve system as an authentication method?
Did you know that in Flexygo you can set the Cl@ve system as an authentication method?
docs.text:
Starting with Flexygo version 6.5, administrators can implement the Cl@ve system as an authentication method. This feature pursues two main goals:

  • Speeding up user access
  • Strengthening security measures

docs.title: Implementation instructions
docs.text:
For the technical details on how to implement this feature, check Flexygo's built-in documentation at:

Help → Connectors → Cl@ve Authentication

docs.title: Did you know you can clone an object's dependencies into the collection's?
Did you know you can clone an object's dependencies into the collection's?
docs.text: Since Flexygo version 4.12.0.X, a feature has been implemented that lets you clone an object's dependencies into the collection.

docs.title: Accessing the feature
docs.text: The feature is accessed through a button added to the edit grid's configuration. Enabling it shows an option to decide the cloning behavior.

docs.title: Available options
docs.text:
• Overwrite the existing dependencies in the edit grid
  • Keep the existing dependencies unchanged, only adding the ones that don't already exist

This feature optimizes the workflow by letting you reuse dependency configurations flexibly, giving you full control over whether previous configurations are replaced or kept intact.

docs.title: Did you know you can clone an object based on another object?
Did you know you can clone an object based on another object?
docs.text: Starting with version 4.9.0.x, you can duplicate objects along with their main configurations: properties, dependencies, relations, presets, views and templates.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Go to the object you want to duplicate
  2. Run the object cloning process
  3. Specify the new object's name
  4. Select which options you want to include in the copy

docs.title: Did you know you can apply an object's security to a combo?
Did you know you can apply an object's security to a combo?
docs.text:
When configuring a combo or dbcombo, there is an option called "Security object". Selecting it applies the security configured on the object itself, avoiding the need to add where clauses in the query.

This feature simplifies configuring access controls by using the security rules already established on the object, without needing to add extra conditions directly in the SQL query.

docs.title: Did you know you can configure combos to allow new values?
Did you know you can configure combos to allow new values?
docs.text: The flx-dbcombo and flx-multicombo components can be configured to allow new values to be added directly through them. When the record is saved, these new values are automatically added to the designated object.

docs.title: Configuration instructions
docs.text:
To enable this feature:

  1. Go to the Allow new values option
  2. Set up the required fields in the corresponding section

docs.title: Did you know you can compare two databases, both in structure and data, using Visual Studio?
Did you know you can compare two databases, both in structure and data, using Visual Studio?
docs.text: Flexygo relies on tools built into Visual Studio that let you perform powerful database comparisons.

docs.title: Schema comparison
docs.text: Going to Tools → SQL Server → New Schema Comparison, you can compare and update two databases, or a database and a Visual Studio project.

docs.title: Data comparison
docs.text: Through Tools → SQL Server → New Data Comparison, users can compare two databases and generate scripts or perform direct updates.

docs.title: Did you know you can get configuration table changes directly from Flexygo?
Did you know you can get configuration table changes directly from Flexygo?
docs.text: Flexygo lets you access the changes made to configuration tables directly from the application.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Access: the option to get configuration table changes can be found in the object list
  2. Setup:
    • Specify the date from which you want to view changes
    • Select the specific tables to review
    • Generate a script with all the changes made

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text: The generated script lets you easily view, review and copy the changes to use them later.

docs.title: Did you know you can build views with information from different databases?
Did you know you can build views with information from different databases?
docs.text: Flexygo can work with multiple databases at the same time through different connection strings. The system uses ConfConnectionString to access tables and functions in the configuration database, while DataConnectionString serves as the main data model.

docs.title: Setting up multiple connections
docs.text:
To add additional connection strings, you need to:

  • Add them to the web.config file
  • Create an entry in the DbConnectionStrings system table

docs.title: Cross-database queries
docs.text:
In Flexygo's data views, you can write your SQL query mixing several data models, simply by naming the connection string, followed by a dot, the schema and the table name.

Syntax:

SQL
LEFT JOIN {~ConfConnectionString~}.dbo.AspNetUsers

Practical example:

SQL
SELECT EMPLOYEE.employee_id, EMPLOYEE.firstname,
       EMPLOYEE.lastname, u.Id as UserId
FROM EMPLOYEE
LEFT JOIN {~ConfConnectionString~}.dbo.AspNetUsers U
  on U.Reference=EMPLOYEE.employee_id

This approach lets you combine employee information with the application's user data in a single view.

docs.title: Did you know you can view, create, edit or delete objects through JS?
Did you know you can view, create, edit or delete objects through JS?
docs.text: You can perform CRUD operations (create, read, update, delete) on objects directly through JavaScript in Flexygo, instead of using SQL processes or DLLs.

docs.title: Key points
docs.text:
• It is essential to call .read() after declaring an object to get its information before performing any action
  • JavaScript functions respect the system's security; if the user lacks permissions, an error message will be shown and the action will not run

docs.title: Code examples
docs.text:
Insert:

JavaScript
function sampleInsert(){
  let obj=new flexygo.obj.Entity('sysTmpTest');
  obj.read();
  obj.data['TestId'].Value = 1;
  obj.data['Descrip'].Value = 'Sample description';
  if(obj.insert()) {
      flexygo.msg.success("Inserted");
  }
}

Update:

JavaScript
function sampleUpdate(){
  let obj=new flexygo.obj.Entity('sysTmpTest','_Test.TestId=1');
  obj.read();
  obj.data['Descrip'].Value = 'Sample description updated';
  if(obj.update()) {
      flexygo.msg.success("Updated");
  }
}

Delete:

JavaScript
function sampleDelete(){
  var obj=new flexygo.obj.Entity('sysTmpTest','_Test.TestId=1');
  if(obj.delete()) {
      flexygo.msg.success("Deleted");
  }
}

docs.title: Did you know you can turn a property into a custom property?
Did you know you can turn a property into a custom property?
docs.text:
Recent versions of Flexygo let you create a custom property based on an existing one through a specific process.

Once this process is complete, the resulting custom property can be used anywhere in the application.

docs.title: Did you know you can set a default filter on a listing that clears itself after the first search?
Did you know you can set a default filter on a listing that clears itself after the first search?
docs.text: This feature helps optimize performance on screens that are frequently used to filter information.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Set a default filter (such as "mine, today's, etc.")
  2. Enable the Remove on first search option

As a result, once the initial filter has been applied, the custom criteria the user sets in later searches will take precedence.

This optimizes the speed of screens that are always used to filter data, since they come with preset parameters that automatically adjust to the user's needs.

docs.title: Did you know we can create users with a preset password?
Did you know we can create users with a preset password?
docs.text: Starting with version 4.0.0.1, Flexygo lets you create users with passwords set administratively.

docs.title: Creation process
docs.text: In the user creation form, select the Set manual password option. You can additionally enable Must change password to require the user to choose a new password after their first login.

docs.title: Main benefit
docs.text:
By setting a password manually from this form, the user will not need to confirm their password by email, since they will be validated automatically with the assigned password.

This feature speeds up user onboarding by avoiding the need for email confirmation, letting the user sign in immediately with the assigned credentials.

docs.title: Did you know you can set a text to confirm the deletion of a record?
Did you know you can set a text to confirm the deletion of a record?
docs.text: Flexygo lets you configure a security mechanism on objects that requires the user to type a confirmation text before deleting a record.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Customization: the confirmation message can be tailored using specific properties of the object
  • Improved security: adds an extra layer of protection against accidental deletions
  • Flexible configuration: managed directly from the object's configuration

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This feature significantly reduces unintended deletions by requiring users to explicitly confirm their record deletion actions, providing greater control over critical data.

docs.title: Did you know you can open any Flexygo screen directly from a link?
Did you know you can open any Flexygo screen directly from a link?
docs.text:
You can access any Flexygo screen directly through a link.

When a user clicks that link, if they are already signed in, the selected screen will open automatically. If they are not authenticated, the system will ask for the access credentials and then redirect the user to the corresponding location.

docs.title: Additional feature
docs.text: You can also perform an automatic sign-in. To do this, the URL must include the access_token parameter along with a valid access code. These codes can be generated through Flexygo's web API.

docs.title: Did you know we can disable module events?
Did you know we can disable module events?
docs.text: Starting with Flexygo version 4.1.0.6, event management became more flexible. In the event creation/edit form you can choose whether it is active or not, letting you prevent that event from running without having to delete it.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Disable events without deleting them: users can disable events on modules without needing to remove them from the system
  • Visibility in the listing: the event list makes it easy to see at a glance which events are active and which are not

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text: This feature provides greater flexibility in event administration, letting you temporarily pause execution without losing the existing configuration.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo has an emergency stop mode?
Did you know Flexygo has an emergency stop mode?
docs.text: Flexygo offers two modes for managing the application's availability.

docs.title: Maintenance mode
docs.text: Administrators can keep the application operational while update tasks are performed.

docs.title: Emergency stop mode
docs.text:
To completely stop an application, you can rename the app_online.htm file to app_offline.htm in the application's root path. This will:

  • Block connections: every connection to the system will be stopped
  • Show a browser message: a page indicating the offline status will be shown

docs.title: Restoring the service
docs.text:
Once maintenance is finished, the original file name is restored and the service resumes automatically.

Important warning

This action will leave the application completely inaccessible.

docs.title: Did you know you can choose which columns to export to Excel?
Did you know you can choose which columns to export to Excel?
docs.text: Just click the Excel export option on any list and it will automatically ask which fields you want to use in the report.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Select the Excel export option from any listing
  2. The system will automatically ask which fields you want to include in the report
  3. Choose the desired fields to customize the exported document

docs.title: Did you know you can easily import/export Excel?
Did you know you can easily import/export Excel?
Importing Excel
docs.text:
To import Excel files, do a basic setup from the imports menu. You need to select:

  • The object to import
  • The process generated for the import
  • The template to use

Once configured, the process will be available in the tools menu to import Excel directly.

docs.title: Exporting Excel
docs.text:
Although listings have a standard export option, it is not ideal for large volumes of data. For that reason, you can create an Excel-type report instead.

The process is simple: specify the desired object and view, and the export will be configured. It will then be available in the object's process menu just like any other report.

docs.title: Did you know you can format a field without memorizing every type?
Did you know you can format a field without memorizing every type?
docs.text: Flexygo includes a wizard tool that makes it easy to add fields to templates, letting you apply the desired format intuitively.

docs.title: Step-by-step process
docs.text:
1. Click the button available next to the template's code
  2. Follow the instructions provided by the wizard

The platform also offers access to the application's icons right below the wizard, providing complementary visual tools for customizing fields without requiring deep technical knowledge of data types.

docs.title: Did you know you can set a pattern for Flexygo's window title?
Did you know you can set a pattern for Flexygo's window title?
docs.text: Among Flexygo's parameters there is an option called WindowsNameStructure that lets you customize how the window's name appears. This feature is particularly useful because it lets the title update dynamically as you navigate through the application.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Title customization: you can define the exact pattern you want for the window's name
  • Dynamic placeholders: the solution supports placeholders representing object attributes or information about the page currently being viewed
  • Intuitive navigation: the title changes automatically as you move between different sections, giving you context about your location within the application

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: The setting is configured through the WindowsNameStructure parameter in Flexygo's settings, letting you build custom patterns that reflect the structure and specific content of each view.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo has a generic search for every object?
Did you know Flexygo has a generic search for every object?
docs.text: Flexygo lets you configure a generic search for any object in the application, a feature that is often overlooked during development.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Enable developer mode
  2. Click the magnifying-glass icon located in the top bar
  3. Set every search field you want for any object in the application

docs.title: Did you know we can generate HTML reports?
Did you know we can generate HTML reports?
docs.text:
You can create reports in Flexygo using an HTML template associated with a specific object. The process involves two main steps:

  1. Create an HTML template for the desired object
  2. Generate a new report selecting the HTML type, the corresponding object and the created template

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text: This feature lets you generate reports quickly and easily without needing tools like Crystal Reports.

docs.title: Did you know you can restrict access to Flexygo by IP?
Did you know you can restrict access to Flexygo by IP?
docs.text: This feature lets you implement IP-address-based access restrictions within the Flexygo platform.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Authorized IP groups: you can define sets of allowed IP addresses
  • Assignment to users: the created groups can be linked to specific user accounts
  • Use cases: useful for restricting access to specific locations only, such as the corporate office

docs.title: How to configure it
docs.text:
1. Go to Security > IP Groups to create the IP address groups
  2. Assign the created groups while managing or editing users in the system

This feature provides an extra layer of security by controlling where authenticated users can access the platform from.

docs.title: Did you know we can import role and user security?
Did you know we can import role and user security?
docs.text:
You can import a security configuration already defined at the role level into another role, without needing to set it up from scratch. The process is simple: go to the new role, run the import security process and select the role you want to get the configuration from.

This same option is also available at the user level.

docs.title: Did you know you can handle Flexygo events with JavaScript?
Did you know you can handle Flexygo events with JavaScript?
docs.text: You can use the flexygo.events.on and flexygo.events.off functions to manage events in Flexygo through JavaScript.

docs.title: Practical example
docs.text:
A common use case is refreshing a module only when the customer has an active status:

  1. Define a callback function that checks specific conditions:
    • Checks whether the sender is an instance of flexygo.obj.Entity
    • Validates that the object's name is "Cliente"
    • Confirms the Activo field has a value of 1
  2. Get the module's HTML element using a query selector
  3. Subscribe the module to the event using flexygo.events.on() with the parameters: the module, the event type ("entity"), the action ("updated") and the callback function

docs.title: Available data
docs.text: When the event runs, the callback's parameter provides data whose sender corresponds to the event's class (for example, flexygo.Process for process events).

docs.title: Did you know you can add JavaScript to the offline application directly from a file?
Did you know you can add JavaScript to the offline application directly from a file?
docs.text: You can include JavaScript code in an offline application by loading it from a physical file.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text: This approach makes the code easier to maintain and allows logic to be reused across different parts of the application.

docs.title: Did you know you can call JavaScript functions from Flexygo's own templates?
Did you know you can call JavaScript functions from Flexygo's own templates?
docs.text:
Flexygo lets you invoke JavaScript functions directly from templates using a specific syntax. To use this feature, write your marker following this pattern: {{myJSFunction(param1, param2, ...)}} and Flexygo will call the function.

The system will automatically process the call and display the result in the template. A useful feature is that if the parameter names match existing fields in the template, the system will automatically convert those parameters to their corresponding values.

docs.title: Did you know you can manage object insert, update and delete actions with JSON procedures?
Did you know you can manage object insert, update and delete actions with JSON procedures?
docs.text:
In recent versions of Flexygo, you can manage object insert, update and delete actions through stored procedures using JSON.

This feature complements the pre-existing option that uses XML to perform these data manipulation operations.

docs.title: Documentation location
docs.text: For detailed information and practical examples about this feature, check Flexygo's built-in help under: Help → Programming → Update types.

docs.title: Did you know every Flexygo instance has a kanban for managing custom boards?
Did you know every Flexygo instance has a kanban for managing custom boards?
docs.text: There is an object called Boards that makes it easy to create multiple custom boards with adjustable columns. Every instance ships with a first board containing the basic development cycle states.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
The Boards tool lets users:

  • Create as many boards as needed
  • Customize the columns according to their specific requirements
  • Access a default board that includes standard development-cycle states

docs.title: Did you know you can set a fixed order for a Kanban's cards?
Did you know you can set a fixed order for a Kanban's cards?
docs.text:
From the kanban's configuration you can define the fields by which cards will be automatically sorted, instead of using the free-form order that comes by default.

For example, cards can always appear organized by priority once this parameter is configured in the system.

This feature lets you customize the kanban's behavior to keep an ordered structure based on specific criteria of the project or workflow being used.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo has keyboard shortcuts?
Did you know Flexygo has keyboard shortcuts?
docs.text:
Flexygo includes three useful keyboard shortcuts:

  • F1: opens the tool's help
  • F2: opens the configuration parameters
  • Ctrl + S: saves changes when the focus is on an edit form

docs.title: Did you know there is a mode for performing maintenance work on the application?
Did you know there is a mode for performing maintenance work on the application?
docs.text: Starting with Flexygo version 5.3, a maintenance mode is available through the update panel.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
Two available options:

  1. Enable maintenance mode for every user except the admin user
  2. Ability to refresh the screens of every user or a specific one

docs.title: Behavior in maintenance mode
docs.text:
• Regular users see a maintenance interface
  • The administrator user keeps full access to the application

docs.title: Disabling the mode
docs.text: To disable maintenance mode, you can use the update panel's own button or click the maintenance window that appears at the top left over the logo.

docs.title: Scheduled maintenance
docs.text: A new setting was added to the Version Update block that lets you schedule future maintenance. When a date is scheduled, a notice appears to every user showing the remaining time.

docs.title: Did you know you can add security to the App's menus?
Did you know you can add security to the App's menus?
docs.text:
From the shield available in the Menus section of the Offline App panel, you can implement access controls based on roles, users and specific permissions. This feature lets you customize the visibility of the different menus depending on the identity of the user who signs in to the application.

This capability makes it easy to selectively hide or show menu options, improving both security and user experience by restricting access to only the functions relevant to each profile.

docs.title: Did you know you can use multiple databases in Flexygo?
Did you know you can use multiple databases in Flexygo?
docs.text: Flexygo can work with more than one data model, even hosted on different servers. This feature lets users create objects against multiple databases and set relations between them without worrying about their source location.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Automatic real-time query generation
  • Compatible with standard products
  • Transparently linking data from different sources

docs.title: Documentation reference
docs.text: For more information, check: Help → Programming → Linked Servers.

docs.title: Did you know you can have more than one account in Flexygo Mobile?
Did you know you can have more than one account in Flexygo Mobile?
docs.text: Flexygo Mobile lets you manage multiple accounts at the same time, with the ability to switch between them without needing a connection.

docs.title: Supported account types
docs.text:
The system supports accounts that can differ in:

  • Different domains
  • Different users
  • Different applications within the same domain

docs.title: Did you know you can enable and disable nodes through a SQL query?
Did you know you can enable and disable nodes through a SQL query?
docs.text: Starting with version 4.5.0.1, Flexygo lets you enable and disable nodes through SQL queries.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The node's configuration includes a new section called Enable that uses a SQL query to determine whether a node should be enabled or disabled.

docs.title: Did you know you can now configure applications' mail and Web Mail accounts with the OAuth 2.0 protocol?
Did you know you can now configure applications' mail and Web Mail accounts with the OAuth 2.0 protocol?
docs.text: Mail accounts used in the Web Mail section can now be configured using the OAuth 2.0 protocol. This capability extends to both Microsoft and Google accounts.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Built-in help: the platform includes built-in assistance for the setup
  • New authentication option: account configuration now shows a new authentication type section
  • Bearer token support: users can configure the new authentication method through the bearer token option

docs.title: Did you know you can create and restore backups of the offline application?
Did you know you can create and restore backups of the offline application?
docs.text: You can back up the database in Flexygo's offline application.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
To access these functions, go to the application's synchronization menu. Once there, turn on the advanced options switch and you will find two main buttons at the bottom of the screen:

  1. Create backup: generates a file with the data currently stored in the application
  2. Restore backup: lets you load a previously created backup file to recover the saved data

This process lets you preserve the application's information and transfer it between devices or restore it when needed.

docs.title: Did you know you can query the offline application's database?
Did you know you can query the offline application's database?
docs.text: The Flexygo application lets you access the database in offline mode through a feature available in the synchronization menu.

docs.title: Accessing the feature
docs.text: To use this feature, go to the app's synchronization menu and turn on the advanced options switch. At the bottom of that screen you will find the Database button.

docs.title: Available features
docs.text:
Once you access this section, you have two options:

  1. Write custom queries using SQLite
  2. Directly select the table you want to query

This feature lets you flexibly query the local database synchronized on your device, making it easier to access information without an internet connection.

docs.title: Did you know you can resize images coming from offline?
Did you know you can resize images coming from offline?
docs.text: Starting with Flexygo version 4.6.0.1, the offline section lets you configure image compression to prevent images from being stored in the database at excessive sizes.

docs.title: Steps to configure compression
docs.text:
1. Go to the wizard for the object that has the image configuration
  1. Navigate to step 7 and open the image configuration
  1. Set values in the compression section using three parameters:
    • Compression: offers four levels: "Nothing", "Low", "Medium" and "High". The last three reduce the size but affect visual quality
    • Maximum width and Maximum height: set limit dimensions for images, keeping the original proportions without exceeding the specified values

This feature optimizes data storage by letting the application automatically resize images captured in offline mode.

docs.title: Did you know you can access the offline app's synchronization history list?
Did you know you can access the offline app's synchronization history list?
docs.text:
Flexygo lets you review the full log of synchronizations performed by the offline application and run them again if problems were detected during the initial process.

This feature provides significant value to users working with Flexygo's offline version. It lets them verify that every synchronization completed successfully and, if not, re-run them without needing to restart the entire synchronization process.

In addition, accessing the synchronization history gives users greater oversight of the updates applied to the application, letting them confirm that data stays continuously up to date.

docs.title: Did you know that in Flexygo you can set the synchronization timeout in the offline app?
Did you know that in Flexygo you can set the synchronization timeout in the offline app?
docs.text:
Flexygo lets you configure the timeout for synchronization in the offline application, improving the user experience and optimizing data transfer.

This feature lets you customize the synchronization intervals between the offline app and the connected database. This makes it possible to adapt the parameters to each organization's particularities, ensuring data is updated quickly and efficiently.

The timeout adjustment is also especially useful in scenarios where the internet connection is poor or unstable. Users can configure these timeouts to ensure the application works without interruptions, allowing for a smoother experience and reliable synchronization in any circumstance and location.

docs.title: Did you know you can enable/disable presets linked to objects?
Did you know you can enable/disable presets linked to objects?
docs.text:
In the latest versions of Flexygo, you can enable/disable presets linked to objects, making it easier to manage stored presets.

This feature lets users more efficiently manage the predefined settings associated with different objects within the Flexygo platform.

docs.title: Did you know you can enable the profiler in the Offline App from anywhere?
Did you know you can enable the profiler in the Offline App from anywhere?
docs.text: Flexygo's offline application includes a profiling tool that you can use from anywhere in the application.

docs.title: Main functions
docs.text:
To access the profiler, you need to know two fundamental functions:

  • flexygo.sql.initProfiler: starts logging all SQL queries and their results
  • flexygo.sql.stopProfiler: stops logging and displays the captured data in the console

docs.title: Filtering results
docs.text:
When working with complex edits that contain multiple dependencies, you can use:

  • flexygo.sql.filterProfiler: lets you search for specific statements in the logged data

This function is case-insensitive by default, but you can change this behavior by passing true as the third parameter if you need a case-sensitive search.

docs.title: Did you know you can use a profiler for the Offline App's queries?
Did you know you can use a profiler for the Offline App's queries?
docs.text: To access the application's profiler, go to the database menu. There you will find a green button that, when pressed, starts logging every SQL statement executed and its results.

docs.title: Steps to use the profiler
docs.text:
1. Start logging: click the green button in the database menu
  2. Navigate: browse to the screen you want to analyze so its statements and results get logged
  3. Stop logging: go back to the database menu and click the red box
  4. View results: every SQL query executed will be shown along with its results

docs.title: Additional feature
docs.text: The profiler includes a filter at the bottom that lets you show only the statements containing specific text, making it easier to search and analyze particular queries.

docs.title: Did you know you can publish the database with just a double-click?
Did you know you can publish the database with just a double-click?
docs.text: Publishing databases in Flexygo can be simplified into a two-step process.

docs.title: Step 1: configure the publish
docs.text: Open the context menu (right-click) and select "Publish". Complete every step of the publish wizard, setting the required parameters.

docs.title: Step 2: save the profile
docs.text: Before clicking the final publish button, select Save Profile As... to store the configuration.

docs.title: Later use
docs.text: Once the profile is saved, publishing becomes much simpler. You only need to double-click the publish profile file to run the process without reconfiguring the parameters every time.

docs.title: Did you know you can generate QR codes with Flexygo?
Did you know you can generate QR codes with Flexygo?
docs.text:
To create QR codes in Flexygo, you just need to add a specific marker in your configuration. The method is very direct: add the marker with the field's name followed by a pipe and the word QR.

This feature lets you generate QR codes easily, directly from the platform, without needing any additional external tools.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo has Radio and Multiple checkbox controls?
Did you know Flexygo has Radio and Multiple checkbox controls?
docs.text:
Flexygo offers UI controls called Radio and Multiple checkbox that work similarly to the combo and multicombo controls.

The main feature that sets these controls apart is their visual presentation: they display every value on screen at once, which can be a good option for letting the user pick an option more quickly when there are only a few values to choose from.

These controls are especially useful when:

  • There is a limited number of available options
  • A faster selection by the user is required
  • A more direct and visual interface is preferred

docs.title: Did you know you can enable and disable an object's relation through a SQL query?
Did you know you can enable and disable an object's relation through a SQL query?
docs.text: Starting with version 4.9.0.1, Flexygo lets you dynamically control relations between objects. The platform introduces a new section called Enable conditions in the relation's configuration.

docs.title: Main feature
docs.text: This feature lets users use SQL queries to determine whether a relation between objects should be active or inactive.

docs.title: Practical application
docs.text: The solution is implemented directly in the configuration parameters of object relations within the Flexygo system, providing greater flexibility in data management and workflows.

docs.title: Did you know you can integrate Flexygo with scales?
Did you know you can integrate Flexygo with scales?
docs.text:
Flexygo supports integration with weighing devices. Users can capture weight data in two ways:

  1. Manual method: pressing a button located in the text field to capture the weight
  2. Automated method: configuring triggers that collect the data automatically

For additional technical details, check the documentation at Help → Connectors → Scales.

docs.title: Did you know you can push events from the server to browsers?
Did you know you can push events from the server to browsers?
docs.text: You can implement a server-to-client event system in Flexygo, letting the server fire notifications to browsers without any user action.

docs.title: Server side (C#)
docs.text:
The process uses an EventHelper class that generates events with the Push class and the Updated type. The available methods are:

  • FireGenericUserEvent(): sends to a specific user
  • FireGenericUserIDEvent(): sends by user ID
  • FireGenericAllUserEvent(): sends to every user

The event includes a sender object with the data to transmit and a masterIdentity identifier.

docs.title: Client side (JavaScript)
docs.text:
Flexygo's event functions are used to capture the notifications:

JavaScript
flexygo.events.on(document, 'push', 'updated', capturar_evento);

The handler function accesses the data through e.sender and validates the event by comparing e.masterIdentity.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text: This mechanism enables automatic actions in browsers without user intervention, ideal for real-time notifications, status updates, or data synchronization between clients.

docs.title: Did you know two Flexygo applications can share a single document management system?
Did you know two Flexygo applications can share a single document management system?
docs.text: It is very common for an enterprise Flexygo and a customer portal to share document management. When both applications are linked to the same ERP, there is no issue. However, when both are Flexygo instances, one can be used as the main repository while the second accesses the shared documents directly.

docs.title: Configuration steps
docs.text:
Step 1 - Application structure

  • A main application with its own database and configuration
  • A second application with its own database and configuration, plus a third connection pointing to the main application's configuration database

Step 2 - Common path

Configure a setting that specifies the common path where shared documents will be stored.

Steps 3-5 - Updating connection strings

Run SQL scripts to change the connections of the following objects and views in the second application:

  • Document
  • Document_Object
  • Document_Version
  • Documents
  • sysDocumentsCategories

These changes point the document objects to the main application's configuration database.

docs.title: Did you know you can access any object's configuration from the sidebar?
Did you know you can access any object's configuration from the sidebar?
docs.text: The Page Config sidebar works by default to configure the object you are currently viewing, but you can change its value to quickly access any other object.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Quick access to configuration: change the value in the sidebar to switch between different objects
  • List icon: gives direct access to the object's listing
  • Plus (+) icon: gives direct access to inserting new records

This feature provides an efficient way for developers to navigate and quickly access different sections of the application without having to go through multiple menu levels.

docs.title: Did you know there's an option to see which users are viewing the same module at the same time?
Did you know there's an option to see which users are viewing the same module at the same time?
docs.text: Starting with Flexygo version 4.9.0.x, a new feature in the module configuration lets you enable visibility of simultaneous users on list, edit, view and kanban type modules.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: When this option is enabled in the module's configuration, an indicator icon appears showing the number of people currently viewing the module. Hovering the cursor over this icon shows a list with the names of every connected user.

docs.title: Applicability
docs.text:
This feature is available on modules of the following types:

  • List
  • Edit
  • View
  • Kanban

docs.title: Did you know you can identify the source of a SQL connection by application?
Did you know you can identify the source of a SQL connection by application?
docs.text:
To analyze the source of the connections to your database, you can filter using the application's name.

Flexygo includes this feature automatically on new installations. If you need to add it to an existing application, you must edit your web.config file and add the Application Name attribute to your connection string.

docs.title: Did you know the offline app's sqllist components can import templates?
Did you know the offline app's sqllist components can import templates?
docs.text: Starting with version 6.4 of the offline application, you can use page templates directly in the flx-sqllist component.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
To use this feature, two attributes must be added to the component:

  • PageName: the page's name
  • ObjectName: the name of the object whose configuration you want to use

The app will get that page's configuration (SQL statement, header, body and footer), but will only use the values that are not explicitly configured in the component.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The system follows a priority hierarchy:

  1. Explicit settings within the component take precedence
  2. The referenced page's settings are applied as default values
  3. This lets you combine custom elements with reusable templates

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text: This feature enables more efficient development by reusing existing templates, letting the flx-sqllist component show listings on different pages without duplicating code.

docs.title: Did you know you can pin the toolbar in place?
Did you know you can pin the toolbar in place?
docs.text: Since Flexygo version 4.9.0.2, you can keep the toolbar fixed at the top while scrolling through a module. To enable this feature, add the sticky-toolbar class to the corresponding module's configuration.

docs.title: Additional features
docs.text: Similarly, you can also pin a listing's header using the sticky-header class. This keeps the header visible while scrolling through the data.

docs.title: Did you know you can review the Offline App's synchronizations from Flexygo?
Did you know you can review the Offline App's synchronizations from Flexygo?
docs.text: From the offline application menu you can access the synchronization history. To do so, just press the button located at the top of the screen.

docs.title: Available features
docs.text:
Once you access the history, you will be able to:

  • View the synchronizations performed
  • Identify the types of synchronization that were run
  • Restart or repeat the synchronization of specific data

docs.title: Did you know you can create template groupings that users can select and reorder?
Did you know you can create template groupings that users can select and reorder?
docs.text: When creating template groupings in a list, you can enable an option called "User can configure groups" directly in the template's configuration.

docs.title: Technical implementation
docs.text:
When this option is enabled, a specific line must be added to the template's header. The proposed code uses an interactive button:

HTML
<button class="btn {{groupButtonActive(this,'IsCollection')}}"
onclick="$(this).closest('flx-list')[0].toggleGroup('IsCollection');">
Object/Collection</button>

The IsCollection parameter must exactly match the group field you want the user to be able to toggle.

docs.title: Expected result
docs.text: After adding one line of code per grouping you want to enable, users will be able to choose which groupings stay active at any given time, providing greater flexibility and interface customization.

docs.title: Did you know you can create a test environment without worrying about the license, thanks to "Set Single User Mode"?
Did you know you can create a test environment without worrying about the license, thanks to "Set Single User Mode"?
docs.text: The Set Single User Mode process lets you set up a test environment with no license limitations.

docs.title: Main purpose
docs.text: This process is especially useful when moving the production database to a test environment, where the license would normally not work due to environment and existing-user differences.

docs.title: Automatic behavior
docs.text:
The process automatically performs the following actions:

  • Generates a new evaluation license
  • Blocks every user except guest, admin and one selected user
  • Allows development with admin and testing with the chosen user according to their profile/role

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
This approach saves every step described above, leaving only the new license to be activated.

Important warning

We recommend verifying that you are indeed working in a test environment that is distinct from production in terms of server, database, configuration and project name.

docs.title: Accessing the process
docs.text:
Only administrators can access it from Admin Area → Object Collection.

During the process you select a user who, along with admin and guest, will remain active.

docs.title: Did you know the offline app can read messages out loud?
Did you know the offline app can read messages out loud?
docs.text: The Flexygo platform includes a text-to-speech capability through the flexygo.ai.textToSpeech function. This tool lets you play back text content out loud.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Customizable text input: specify any text content you want to be read out loud
  • Language setting: it defaults to the user's language, but it can be changed manually
  • Speed control: adjust the playback speed to your preference
  • Volume control: adjust the playback's volume level

docs.title: Did you know you can install Flexygo unattended from the command line?
Did you know you can install Flexygo unattended from the command line?
docs.text:
Flexygo lets you run installations without a graphical interface using command-line parameters. To view every available option, run:

Text Only
./FlexygoInstaller.exe /?

docs.title: CRM installation example
docs.text:
Below is a sample command to install a CRM system:

Text Only
./FlexygoInstaller.exe /unatended /r:"https://nuget.flexygo.com/nuget"
/p:"FlexygoCRM" /pn:"NombreCliente_CRM" /ap:"MyAdminPassword"
/virtualPath:"/CRM" /phisicalPath:"c:\Webs\CRM" /confDB:"CRM_IC"
/confDBu:"sa" /confDBp:"-a123456" /confDBh:"localhost"
/dataDB:"concello" /dataDBu:"sa" /dataDBp:"-a123456"
/dataDBh:"localhost" /mailAdmin:"admin@mycompany.com"
/mailHost:"mail.mycompany.com" /mailUser:"MymailUser"
/mailPass:"MyMailPassword" /mailPort:"25" /mailSSL:"true"

This approach enables fully automating the installation process without any manual intervention in the graphical interface.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo added a new signature control integrated with Wacom tablets?
Did you know Flexygo added a new signature control integrated with Wacom tablets?
docs.text: Flexygo has developed a new control type, similar to the WhiteBoard, that lets you work with Wacom tablets to capture signatures.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
Configuration:

  • A new control type called Wacom Signature
  • Configured as an object property or process parameter

  • Available in the Options section

Functionality:

The system lets you save both the signature and the biometric data captured through the Wacom tablets, making it easier to integrate digital signatures into Flexygo's processes.

docs.title: Did you know you can reuse the WebAPI's authorization tokens?
Did you know you can reuse the WebAPI's authorization tokens?
docs.text: By default, Flexygo generates a new token on every request to the /token endpoint. However, this behavior can be changed.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
For the system to return the same token while it remains valid, you need to:

  1. Go to the application's parameters
  2. Enable the ReuseToken option

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Once this setting is enabled, as long as a token stays "alive" it will be returned on every request. This optimizes performance by reusing valid tokens instead of constantly generating new ones.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo has webhooks?
Did you know Flexygo has webhooks?
docs.text:
Flexygo can receive events from external services regardless of their transmission protocol.

This feature enables secure integration with third-party services. For example, it can be used to securely receive notification of when a user completes a payment and start shipping an order.

docs.title: What is Flexygo's SBOM and why do we publish it?
What is Flexygo's SBOM and why do we publish it?
docs.text:
At Flexygo we maintain an ongoing commitment to the transparency, security and trust that our customers place in us. With that goal in mind, we have decided to publish our platform's SBOM (Software Bill of Materials), a document that details all the software components — both our own and third-party — that are part of the solutions built with Flexygo.

An SBOM can be understood as the digital equivalent of a bill of materials in manufacturing. In a software context, this document structurally records every library, module and dependency involved in developing, running and maintaining an application. This provides a complete view of the product's technical composition, which is essential to guarantee its traceability and strengthen the security of the digital supply chain.

Publishing the SBOM follows an increasingly widespread practice in the technology industry, driven by the growing need to control the risks associated with external dependencies and to comply with new international standards on cybersecurity and regulatory compliance. Bodies such as the United States' National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) and the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) actively promote the adoption of SBOMs as a key tool to increase the transparency and resilience of computer systems.

With this in mind, the decision to publish Flexygo's SBOM pursues three main objectives. First, guaranteeing transparency, giving our customers, auditors and partners the ability to know precisely which components make up the platform. This information enables compliance analysis, license verification and technological compatibility checks with other environments. Second, strengthening security, by making it easier to detect and manage vulnerabilities associated with external dependencies or outdated versions. Having an up-to-date SBOM makes it possible to act quickly on security alerts and apply preventive measures effectively. And third, meeting regulatory and technology-governance requirements, which are becoming increasingly strict in both the public and private sectors.

Having an audited SBOM demonstrates a genuine commitment to secure development best practices and to the traceability of software throughout its entire lifecycle.

Publishing our SBOM is not a simple transparency gesture, but a strategic measure that strengthens trust in the Flexygo platform. It represents a decisive step towards a more open, verifiable and sustainable development model, where users can have full certainty about the origin, licensing and security of every component. It also lets us improve our own internal quality-control, version-management and dependency-monitoring processes, strengthening the foundation on which our technology solutions evolve.

In short, publishing Flexygo's SBOM reflects our commitment to responsible innovation and technical excellence. We believe that transparency and traceability are not merely regulatory obligations, but fundamental values that help build a more trustworthy, secure and collaborative digital ecosystem.

docs.title: Attachment
docs.text: You can download Flexygo's SBOM in CycloneDX (JSON) format.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: The purpose of this document is to establish recommendations and best practices for a secure Flexygo installation on an IIS environment, minimizing vulnerabilities and ensuring the protection of associated data and services.

docs.title: 2. Recommended architecture
docs.text:
• Web server (IIS): dedicated exclusively to Flexygo and its associated web services.
  • Database server (SQL Server): a separate instance from IIS, not exposed externally. It should only be accessible from the internal network or via VPN.
  • File server (NAS): a repository external to the website where the documents managed by Flexygo will be stored.

docs.title: 3.1. Installation location
docs.text:
• Install Flexygo in a separate folder from IIS's standard structure (C:\inetpub\wwwroot).
    • Recommended example: D:\WebApps\Flexygo
  • Assign the minimum necessary permissions to the Application Pool account (Read, Execute).

docs.title: 3.2. IIS security configuration
docs.text:
• Disable directory listing (Directory Browsing).

  • Remove server headers: in web.config or through the URL Rewrite module:

    XML
    <outboundRules>
  <rule name="Remove Server Header">
    <match serverVariable="RESPONSE_Server" pattern=".+" />
    <action type="Rewrite" value="" />
  </rule>
</outboundRules>

  • Enable Request Filtering to block unnecessary extensions (.cmd, .bat, .exe, .dll).

docs.title: 4. External document management
docs.text:
• Configure Flexygo so that document storage does not reside within the IIS website.
  • Use a dedicated NAS or file server, accessible only from the internal network.
  • Implement secure SMB or NFS authentication.
  • Control access through specific NTFS permissions or ACLs.

docs.title: 5. Database (SQL Server)
docs.text:
• Install on a separate server, preferably on an internal subnet with no direct Internet access.
  • Disable "sa" authentication and enable Windows authentication whenever possible, and create a dedicated user for Flexygo.
  • Restrict access ports through an internal firewall.

docs.title: 6. HTTPS and SSL/TLS certificates
docs.text:
• Install a valid SSL certificate issued by a trusted CA.
  • Force HTTPS across the whole site (301 redirection from HTTP).
  • Configure TLS 1.2 or higher, disabling SSL 2.0, SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0.

docs.title: 7. Additional hardening
docs.text:
• Regularly update IIS, .NET, Windows and Flexygo.
  • Implement a web application firewall (WAF) if available (e.g. ModSecurity or Azure WAF).
  • Enable detailed logging (IIS Logs + Event Viewer + Flexygo logs).
  • Implement automatic backups (web, NAS and database).
  • Enable monitoring and alerts for suspicious access.
  • Enable MFA either in Flexygo itself or in the delegated authentication system.

docs.title: 1. Principle of least privilege (mandatory)
docs.text:
Every object, process or customization MUST be created applying the principle of least privilege.

  • Explicitly define roles with access and their read, write and delete permissions
  • Avoid objects accessible by all users.
  • Do not rely on button visibility as a security control.
  • Block direct execution by URL when it should not be allowed.
  • Do not expose unnecessary objects in the API.

docs.title: 2. Integrating Flexygo into a CI/CD cycle
docs.text:
Flexygo must be integrated into a CI/CD pipeline to guarantee ongoing quality and security.

  • Version control through NuGet packages.
  • Use centralized repositories (Git).
  • Define a Hotfix policy.

docs.title: 3. Including tests in CI/CD
docs.text:
Every development must include automated tests, adapted to Flexygo's low-code nature.

  • Develop interface tests to ensure full functionality and access.
  • Unit tests to test DLLs or stored procedures.
  • Include running Flexygo's native tests to verify the tool's structure.
  • Add load tests if you'll be working in environments with many users.

docs.title: 4. Protecting passwords and secrets
docs.text:
It is mandatory to ensure that no password or secret leaves the system.

Forbidden:

  • Hardcoding passwords in code, SQL or configuration.
  • Sending credentials through logs or error messages.
  • Committing passwords to source control.

Mandatory:

  • Add pipeline checks that:
    • Look for secret patterns in the code.
    • Block the deployment if any are detected.

docs.title: 5.1 Enabling auditing
docs.text:
Enable auditing on every object that:

  • Handles sensitive data
  • Allows critical changes
  • Affects key business processes

docs.title: 6. Secure DLL development
docs.text: When developing custom DLLs, the following rules must be strictly followed.

docs.title: 6.1 Database access
docs.text:
Use exclusively:

  • Parameterized SQL
  • Stored Procedures

Dynamic SQL built by string concatenation is forbidden.

❌ Incorrect:

C#
string sql = "SELECT * FROM Clientes WHERE Id = " + id;

✅ Correct:

C#
SqlCommand cmd = new SqlCommand("GetClienteById", conn);
cmd.CommandType = CommandType.StoredProcedure;
cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@Id", id);

docs.title: 7. Pre-production review checklist
docs.text:
Before deploying to production, make sure you meet these points:

  • [ ] Least privilege is applied to all objects
  • [ ] Flexygo is integrated into CI/CD
  • [ ] Tests run successfully in the pipeline
  • [ ] No passwords or secrets are exposed
  • [ ] Auditing is enabled where appropriate
  • [ ] DLLs use parameterized SQL or stored procedures

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
The Flexygo project implements a formally structured Secure Development Lifecycle (SDLC), integrating security practices, quality control and traceability into every phase of the build, integration and deployment process. The continuous integration (CI/CD) system documents and runs more than 30 automated steps that ensure the integrity, availability and security of the software at every stage of the development cycle.

The automation environment guarantees that every build follows a reproducible flow, with security controls, code analysis, unit tests, secure packaging and periodic artifact backups.

docs.title: 2. General flow of the applied SDLC
docs.text:
Flexygo's development process is structured into sequential stages with dependencies conditioned on the success of the previous steps, guaranteeing a secure, error-free flow before reaching the publishing environment.

Main phases:

  1. Environment preparation and cleanup
  2. Controlled code build
  3. Secure dependency management
  4. Validation and unit tests
  5. Quality and coverage analysis
  6. Artifact generation and publishing
  7. Automated technical documentation
  8. Version backup and retention
  9. Secure configuration closure

Each phase includes verifiable controls and evidence demonstrating the application of security and quality measures.

docs.title: 3.1. Environment preparation (steps 1–2)
docs.text:
• Cleaning connection strings in web.config: the automated process runs a PowerShell script that removes or masks sensitive connection strings before starting the build, preventing accidental credential exposure. This control ensures compliance with the principle of minimizing sensitive information in development environments.
  • Source code backup: before building, an automated backup of the source code is made, preserving a restore point in case of later alterations or errors. The backup mechanism is conditioned on the success of the previous steps, ensuring only valid versions are stored.

docs.title: 3.2. Build and dependency management (steps 3–6)
docs.text:
• NuGet package restoration: packages are obtained from controlled sources, with verified and locked versions to ensure the reproducibility and integrity of the build environment.
  • Solution build (.NET / MSBuild): the project is built automatically using MSBuild, ensuring full traceability from source code to the generated binary.
  • Publishing configurations and databases (CONFIG DB and DATA DB): the publishing scripts use SQLPACKAGE and run controlled build processes, only validated if the previous steps succeeded, applying the principle of build-chain integrity.

docs.title: 3.3. Testing, validation and technical auditing (steps 11–14, 23–25, 30)
docs.text:
• Building and running service and interface tests: unit tests are run using Visual Studio Test (VSTest), integrated into the pipeline. These tests verify the functionality of the main modules and the interoperability between services. Test results are automatically collected and analyzed to assess compliance with quality criteria.
  • Code coverage: the system uses JetBrains dotCover to collect coverage metrics, allowing the degree of test validation of the code to be measured. This step only runs if the build succeeds, avoiding reports on inconsistent versions.

  • Static code analysis (SonarQube): although some analyses appear disabled in the screenshots, the SDLC process considers their execution part of the full cycle. The TypeScript, T-SQL and VB modules are audited for vulnerabilities, poor practices or insecure code. This provides evidence of compliance with the static analysis controls of OWASP SAMM and ISO/IEC 27034.

docs.title: 3.4. Artifact and documentation generation (steps 16–22)
docs.text:
• Automated changelog: generated through PowerShell, ensuring traceability between versions and facilitating change audits.
  • Secure packaging (ZIP APP, ZIP DOCU, NuGet package): artifacts are packaged automatically and versioned, including a build number and an internal digital signature. This process guarantees the non-repudiation and integrity of the distributed artifacts.

  • Automatic technical documentation generation: three types of documentation are generated:

    • JS: through Node.js (YUIDoc)
    • VB: through GhostDoc
    • SQL: through TeamCity SQLDoc

    This ensures documentation consistency and technical traceability between code and documentation.

docs.title: 3.5. Backup and configuration control (step 26 and 12–15)
docs.text:
• Post-publication backup copy: automatic copies are generated after publishing each build, ensuring the preservation of final artifacts and deployment evidence.
  • Configuration file management: the system cleans and replaces config files at different points of the pipeline (start and close) to ensure that:
    • No credentials or keys are exposed in test environments.
    • Sensitive configurations stay out of source control.

docs.title: 3.6. Dynamic security scanning and validation (SecDevOps)
docs.text:
The SecDevOps pipeline, integrated within the development cycle, is responsible for validating the software's resilience against vulnerabilities and exploits before it is published. The flow includes the following automated steps:

  1. Download the installer: retrieves the latest compiled version of the software from the internal repositories, ensuring tests run against the final version rather than intermediate environments.
  2. Install Flexygo: automates installing the application in an isolated test environment that replicates the production infrastructure.
  3. Run exploit (automated security testing): a Python script (flexygoscan.py) is run that performs controlled penetration tests against the deployed instance. These tests include validations of authentication, SQL injection, XSS and session manipulation, serving as evidence of an active dynamic application security testing (DAST) process.
  4. Uninstall Flexygo: the test environment is automatically cleaned up once the analysis finishes, ensuring no execution artifacts or sensitive data remain.
  5. Delete the test database: as the final phase, the database used during the tests is securely deleted, preserving confidentiality and preventing information exposure.

This process constitutes key evidence of operational security, demonstrating that Flexygo applies active controls for early vulnerability detection before releasing versions.

docs.title: 3.7. Artifact publishing and distribution control
docs.text:
The final publishing flow includes validating and deploying NuGet packages to authenticated repositories:

  1. Publishing internal and external NuGet artifacts:
    • Ahora's corporate repository (nuget.ahorabh.com)
    • Microsoft's official NuGet repository (nuget.org)
  2. Each publication is conditioned on the successful completion of all previous steps, ensuring that only verified and audited artifacts are distributed.
  3. Marking artifacts as "pinned": the final PowerShell process locks critical versions in the internal repository, preventing their accidental deletion or overwriting. This control ensures the traceability and availability of certified versions.

docs.title: 4. Audits and traceability
docs.text:
Every SDLC stage is logged in the continuous integration system, making it possible to audit:

  • Execution times
  • Test results
  • Build and publishing logs
  • Generated versions
  • Configuration changes

The pipeline prevents moving on to the next phase if a step doesn't run correctly, which constitutes a security flow control and evidence of compliance with DevSecOps best practices.

docs.title: 5. Conclusions
docs.text:
Flexygo's secure development model incorporates security, control and traceability mechanisms across the entire software lifecycle. The evidence shows the systematic application of information protection measures, version control, code auditing and artifact validation.

This process complies with the principles of a secure SDLC, aligned with international standards such as OWASP SAMM, ISO/IEC 27034 and NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF), providing guarantees of integrity, traceability and security for the software produced.

docs.title: Vulnerability management
docs.text: At Flexygo, vulnerability management is a key process within the secure development lifecycle (SecDevOps). This process ensures early detection, assessment, prioritization and remediation of vulnerabilities present in the code or in deployment environments, guaranteeing the integrity, availability and confidentiality of applications.

docs.title: 1. Vulnerability detection with SonarQube
docs.text:
Flexygo uses SonarQube as its main tool for static code analysis. This system is integrated directly into the development pipelines and performs the following functions:

  • Automatic analysis of the source code on every commit or pull request, detecting vulnerabilities, code smells and poor security practices.
  • Quality assessment based on OWASP security rules and international standards (CWE, SANS).
  • Risk report generation, reviewed by the development and security team before approving integration into the main environment.
  • Alerts and metrics: SonarQube automatically notifies the people responsible when critical or blocking vulnerabilities are detected.

docs.title: 2. Integration with the SecDevOps cycle
docs.text:
The SecDevOps strategy implemented at Flexygo ensures that security is present from the earliest stages of development. Its key principles include:

  • Shift-Left Security: detection and remediation happen in early development phases, reducing cost and time.
  • Test automation: CI/CD pipelines automatically run security analyses and pre-deployment validations, launching attack scripts against every final version.
  • Multidisciplinary collaboration: development, operations and security teams work together to ensure vulnerabilities are managed efficiently and transparently.

docs.title: 3. Remediation and deployment with GitFlow and Hotfix
docs.text:
If a critical vulnerability is detected in production, a structured remediation flow based on GitFlow is followed:

  1. Creating a Hotfix branch: a specific branch is created from main or release to address the issue without interfering with ongoing development.
  2. Fix and validation: the development team implements the fix and re-runs the SonarQube analyses to verify the patch's effectiveness.
  3. Immediate deployment (Hotfix): once the fix is validated, it is deployed immediately to the production environment through the automated pipeline.
  4. Controlled merge: the Hotfix branch is then merged into develop and main, ensuring the fixed code is synchronized across all active branches.

docs.title: 4. Mitigation and preventive measures
docs.text:
In addition to detection and remediation processes, Flexygo implements active mitigation mechanisms that protect the environment in real time against exploitation attempts. The system monitors every incoming request, analyzing its parameters and behavior. If a suspicious pattern or signs of an attack are identified — such as code injection, header manipulation or unauthorized access attempts — the request is blocked immediately. Likewise, if five suspicious requests from the same IP are detected within a minute, the system automatically blocks that IP address as a preventive measure.

Additionally, to prevent brute-force attacks, Flexygo applies a temporary user lockout after five failed authentication attempts, preventing repeated access attempts and significantly reducing the risk of credential compromise. These measures, combined with early detection and automated response, strengthen the overall security posture of the Flexygo ecosystem.

Every certified product must be built starting from Flexygo as a NuGet package; development built on top of another Flexygo product will not be certified.
